decisions.rationale: Claim reproduced on a scratch copy of the commit 30cd7583 snapshot with the private solution applied. The solution passes 8/8. With the overview loading paragraph changed to "Loading services…" (typographic ellipsis) or "Loading services" (no dots), t5 passes but t6 fails with "Unable to find an element with the text: Loading services...." inside the abort test, so the two tests disagree about the same screen and a wording mismatch is misreported as an abort problem. The TASK 5 comment does give the exact text, which is why this is low. The finding is valid and would be accepted, but workflow.md 2.4 allows only two correction loops, both are used, and a third escalates. Escalated for that reason only. Recommended resolution: change t6 line 45 from getByText("Loading services...") to getByText(/Loading services/), matching t5 line 29, so t5 alone owns the wording check and t6 keeps only what the abort check needs. Verified on the scratch copy: with that one-line change the solution passes 8/8, the typographic-ellipsis variant passes t5 and t6, the sme-err-r1 mutant (no AbortError guard, error cleared on success) still fails t6 at the no-error assertion, and the shipped starter still fails t6 at "expected null not to be null". This is a reversible, in-scope correction: a test-only, assertion-loosening edit with no change to test names, failingTests, expected/on-completion.txt, objectives or minutes. It does stale the solved run, the critic bindings for that file and the module lock. If the captain authorises it, re-run the solved run, regenerate the lock and have the education critic recheck only edu-err-s1. The alternative is to ship as-is and record edu-err-s1 as a known low, since the TASK 5 comment states the exact text.
